content:
Let \(x_i\) be the number of chocolate chip cookies in the \(67\)-cookie block starting at position \(i\). Consecutive blocks share \(66\) cookies, so
\[
|x_{i+1}-x_i|\le 1.
\]
Over all \(100\) starting positions, the total number of chocolate chip appearances is
\[
53\cdot 67=3551,
\]
so the average is \(35.51\). Hence some block has at most \(35\) chocolate chip cookies, and some block has at least \(36\). Since adjacent block counts change by at most \(1\), moving around the circle from the former block to the latter must pass through both \(35\) and \(36\). Thus \(k=35\) and \(k=36\) are always guaranteed.

To see no other \(k\) is guaranteed, arrange the \(47\) oatmeal cookies as evenly as possible, for example at positions
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{100j}{47}\right\rfloor \pmod{100},\quad j=0,1,\dots,46.
\]
Then every \(67\)-cookie block contains either \(31\) or \(32\) oatmeal cookies, hence exactly \(35\) or \(36\) chocolate chip cookies. So no other value of \(k\) is forced.

Thus the guaranteed values are \(35\) and \(36\), and their sum is
\[
35+36=71.
\]
\[
\boxed{71}
\]
